title: Slot-based microbatch admission with predictive headroom and KV eviction scoring
creator: Maya Chen
description: High-QPS tails cause repeated microbatch saturation and inefficient KV cache churn. This ticket implements a slot-based soft-lease admission controller that combines a predictive headroom estimator with per-priority slot quotas, KV eviction scoring, and a multi-level backpressure signal to reduce tail latency and GPU OOM risk while preserving throughput.
background: Observed in production: frequent short-lived spikes at p99.9 where microbatches fill GPU slots quickly, causing eviction storms in the KV cache and repeated model recompute due to KV misses. Existing threshold-based admission causes oscillation: when admission opens, a flood of small requests spikes memory use; when it closes, latency increases for higher-priority requests. Prior attempts (fixed ceilings, simple EWMA headroom) reduced some spikes but didn't adapt to changing sequence length distributions or priority mixes.
proposed_solution:
1) Introduce token-slot soft leases: each request consumes a number of slots proportional to estimated tokens (seq_len_est * slot_scale). Slots allocated from a per-GPU bucket with per-priority subquotas (realtime, default, background). Leases expire with TTL; long-running requests refresh their lease only if token consumption remains within predicted bounds.

2) Predictive headroom estimator: maintain a lightweight EWMA histogram of recently observed sequence lengths and token emission rates per model-type and region. Use this to compute a 95th-percentile slot reservation and a dynamic safety margin (alpha) that adjusts with observed variance.

3) KV eviction scoring: when headroom is low, evict KV entries using a scored policy that blends recency, frequency, and predicted reuse probability (from a short-term reuse model). Score = w1*recency_rank + w2*freq_score + w3*(1 - reuse_prob). Tune weights to favor keeping recent conversational contexts and high-reuse embeddings.

4) Layered backpressure outputs: (a) soft-admit delay (randomized small delay to smooth bursts), (b) token-shedding hint for very long requests (server may request client to truncate prefix when safe), (c) priority preemption: background slots can be preempted after a grace period.

5) Safety fallbacks: when eviction cannot free slots fast enough, fall back to model variant with lower KV footprint or reject low-priority requests with 429 and a Retry-After header.

6) Observability: per-slot telemetry, per-priority queue lengths, eviction counts and post-eviction miss-rate, and p50/p95/p99 latency deltas for affected routes.
design_decisions:
- Use soft leases (TTL refresh) to prevent head-of-line blocking from long queued requests.
- Keep slot accounting token-centric (not request-count) to adapt to varied seq lengths.
- Predictive estimator prioritized 95th percentile to avoid tuning to mean only; alpha adapts by variance.
- KV eviction scoring uses short-term ML reuse predictor (lightweight logistic reg) trained on last 1-5 minutes of accesses; avoids cold-modeling.
- Prefer randomized admission delay over immediate hard reject to avoid synchronized retry storms.
acceptance_criteria:
- Admission controller reduces p99.9 latency spikes by at least 30% on the synthetic high-QPS trace used in validation.
- KV miss storm count (evictions that cause downstream recompute within 2s) reduced by 25%.
- GPU memory headroom variance reduced (stddev) by 20% during 10 minute synthetic bursts.
- Observability dashboard shows per-slot and per-priority metrics; rollout runbook attached.
- End-to-end integration test and canary in staging passing for 48h with no OOM incidents.
implementation_notes:
- Implement slot allocator in the admission layer near queuing. Keep lock-free counters where possible; use CAS on 64-bit counters for slot pools.
- Maintain per-model-type histograms using compact sliding-window sketches to limit memory.
- KV eviction scoring will be pluggable; start with heuristic weights and enable a fast logistic reuse predictor as opt-in.
- Add feature flags: slot_admission_v1, kv_eviction_scoring_v1, headroom_predictor_v1.
- Instrument granular metrics and add high-cardinality labels sparingly (model-type, region, priority).
- Ensure compatibility with Dedicated mode where GPUs are isolated but slot pool sizing differs; expose configuration knobs for reserved capacity.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (dev/staging): feature flags on, run synthetic high-QPS traces, collect metrics (1 week).
Phase 2 (canary): enable on a single shard in us-west with 10% traffic and monitor 72h. Auto-disable conditions: OOMs, spike >50% in p99 latency, eviction storms > baseline.
Phase 3 (gradual): ramp to 30% then 60% over a week with instrumentation dashboards.
Phase 4 (global): enable with tuned parameters; create runbook for rollback.
Post-rollout: run A/B experiment comparing default vs slot-based over 14 days for cost and latency delta.
metrics:
- p50/p95/p99/p99.9 latency by priority and route (baseline vs candidate).
- KV eviction rate (evictions/min) and post-eviction cache-miss multiplier.
- GPU free memory headroom distribution and stddev.
- Admission rejections (429) and token-shedding hints issued.
- Throughput (tokens/sec) and tail latency cost per 1M tokens.
- Canary anomaly detector alerts (OOM, error-rate spike, latency regression).
tests:
- Unit tests for slot accounting (concurrent alloc/free).
- Deterministic simulation harness that replays traces with varying seq length distributions and priority mixes. Expect simulated reductions in eviction storms.
- Integration test: admission controller + KV with a small in-memory KV simulator to validate eviction scoring behavior.
- e2e staging: 48h synthetic high-QPS soak with canary thresholds enforced.
- Load test: 1M reqs/hour with 10% long-tail (seq>2048) requests to verify graceful degradation.
risks:
- Overly aggressive eviction scoring could increase recompute latency if reuse predictor misfires.
- Incorrect headroom alpha tuning could either be too conservative (wasting capacity) or too permissive (risking OOMs).
- Complexity increases in admission path may add small fixed CPU overhead; verify at scale.
- Interactions with Dedicated reserved capacity must be validated to avoid violating SLAs.
notes:
- Preliminary simulation (2025-02-25) showed 35% reduction in simulated eviction storms with conservative parameters.
- We will expose per-tenant knobs for Dedicated customers wanting stricter isolation.
- Consider future enhancement: adaptive slot_scale per-model based on quantization profile.
